steps.title: Old levels have memory
steps.text:
When price breaks **up** through resistance, that level often turns into **support** when price comes back to it.

And when support breaks **down**, it often becomes **resistance**. This is called **role reversal**.

steps.title: Why it happens
steps.text:
Traders remember prices. Sellers who were caught on the wrong side of the breakout may buy back near the old level to get out at break-even. Traders who missed the move wait for a return to the level to buy.

Together they add buying pressure right at the old ceiling.

steps.title: Break and retest
steps.text:
On this chart, price broke above resistance, came **back** to it and bounced. That return to the level is called a **retest**.

Retests give a clear place to enter, with a nearby, logical stop.

steps.question: Price breaks below a support zone, then rallies back up into it. What might that zone do now?
steps.explanation: Broken support often turns into **resistance**. It's a tendency, not a law, so trades still need a stop.

steps.prompt: Tap the candle where price broke out of the range.
steps.explanation: The breakout candle is the first one that **closes above** the range's resistance. Wicks poking through don't count until a candle closes beyond the level.

steps.title: Not every retest holds
steps.text:
Sometimes price slices straight back through the level and the breakout fails.

That's why a retest trade still needs a stop: for a buy, usually **just below the retested zone**. If price closes back inside the old range, the idea was wrong.

steps.question: You buy a retest of old resistance, which is now acting as support. Where does your stop-loss go?
options: In the middle of the zone
No stop needed: role reversal always works
steps.explanation: If price falls back **below** the zone, the level didn't hold, so that's where the trade idea is wrong.

points: Broken resistance often becomes **support**, and broken support **resistance**.
A return to the broken level is a **retest**.
A breakout needs a **close** beyond the level.
Retests can fail: keep a **stop** beyond the zone.
